units.title: Title
units.text: Identify the report as a systematic review, meta-analysis, or both

units.title: Structured summary
units.text: Provide a structured summary including, as applicable, background, objectives, data sources, study eligibility criteria, participants, interventions, study appraisal and synthesis methods, results, limitations, conclusions and implications of key findings, systematic review registration number

units.title: Rationale
units.text: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of what is already known

units.title: Objectives
units.text: Provide an explicit statement of questions being addressed with reference to participants, interventions, comparisons, outcomes, and study design (PICOS)

units.title: Protocol and registration
units.text: Indicate if a review protocol exists, if and where it can be accessed (such as web address), and, if available, provide registration information including registration number

units.title: Eligibility criteria
units.text: Specify study characteristics (such as PICOS, length of follow-up) and report characteristics (such as years considered, language, publication status) used as criteria for eligibility, giving rationale

units.title: Information sources
units.text: Describe all information sources (such as databases with dates of coverage, contact with study authors to identify additional studies) in the search and date last searched

units.title: Search
units.text: Present full electronic search strategy for at least one database, including any limits used, such that it could be repeated

units.title: Study selection
units.text: State the process for selecting studies (that is, screening, eligibility, included in systematic review, and, if applicable, included in the meta-analysis)

units.title: Data collection process
units.text: Describe method of data extraction from reports (such as piloted forms, independently, in duplicate) and any processes for obtaining and confirming data from investigators

units.title: Data items
units.text: List and define all variables for which data were sought (such as PICOS, funding sources) and any assumptions and simplifications made

units.title: Risk of bias in individual studies
units.text: Describe methods used for assessing risk of bias of individual studies (including specification of whether this was done at the study or outcome level), and how this information is to be used in any data synthesis

units.title: Summary measures
units.text: State the principal summary measures (such as risk ratio, difference in means).

units.title: Synthesis of results
units.text: Describe the methods of handling data and combining results of studies, if done, including measures of consistency (such as I2) for each meta-analysis

units.title: Risk of bias across studies
units.text: Specify any assessment of risk of bias that may affect the cumulative evidence (such as publication bias, selective reporting within studies)

units.title: Additional analyses
units.text: Describe methods of additional analyses (such as sensitivity or subgroup analyses, meta-regression), if done, indicating which were pre-specified

units.title: Study selection
units.text: Give numbers of studies screened, assessed for eligibility, and included in the review, with reasons for exclusions at each stage, ideally with a flow diagram

units.title: Study characteristics
units.text: For each study, present characteristics for which data were extracted (such as study size, PICOS, follow-up period) and provide the citations

units.title: Risk of bias within studies
units.text: Present data on risk of bias of each study and, if available, any outcome-level assessment (see item 12).

units.title: Results of individual studies
units.text: For all outcomes considered (benefits or harms), present for each study (a) simple summary data for each intervention group and (b) effect estimates and confidence intervals, ideally with a forest plot

units.title: Synthesis of results
units.text: Present results of each meta-analysis done, including confidence intervals and measures of consistency

units.title: Risk of bias across studies
units.text: Present results of any assessment of risk of bias across studies (see item 15)

units.title: Additional analysis
units.text: Give results of additional analyses, if done (such as sensitivity or subgroup analyses, meta-regression [see item 16])

units.title: Summary of evidence
units.text: Summarise the main findings including the strength of evidence for each main outcome; consider their relevance to key groups (such as health care providers, users, and policy makers)

units.title: Limitations
units.text: Discuss limitations at study and outcome level (such as risk of bias), and at review level (such as incomplete retrieval of identified research, reporting bias)

units.title: Conclusions
units.text: Provide a general interpretation of the results in the context of other evidence, and implications for future research

units.title: Funding
units.text: Describe sources of funding for the systematic review and other support (such as supply of data) and role of funders for the systematic review

units.title: Title
units.text: Identify the report as a systematic review.

units.title: Abstract
units.text: See the PRISMA 2020 for Abstracts checklist (table 2).

units.title: Rationale
units.text: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of existing knowledge.

units.title: Objectives
units.text: Provide an explicit statement of the objective(s) or question(s) the review addresses.

units.title: Eligibility criteria
units.text: Specify the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the review and how studies were grouped for the syntheses.

units.title: Information sources
units.text: Specify all databases, registers, websites, organisations, reference lists and other sources searched or consulted to identify studies. Specify the date when each source was last searched or consulted.

units.title: Search strategy
units.text: Present the full search strategies for all databases, registers and websites, including any filters and limits used.

units.title: Selection process
units.text: Specify the methods used to decide whether a study met the inclusion criteria of the review, including how many reviewers screened each record and each report retrieved, whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.

units.title: Data collection process
units.text: Specify the methods used to collect data from reports, including how many reviewers collected data from each report, whether they worked independently, any processes for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.

units.title: Data items
units.text: List and define all outcomes for which data were sought. Specify whether all results that were compatible with each outcome domain in each study were sought (e.g. for all measures, time points, analyses), and if not, the methods used to decide which results to collect.

units.title: Study risk of bias assessment
units.text: Specify the methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies, including details of the tool(s) used, how many reviewers assessed each study and whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.

units.title: Effect measures
units.text: Specify for each outcome the effect measure(s) (e.g. risk ratio, mean difference) used in the synthesis or presentation of results.

units.title: Synthesis methods
units.text: Describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis (e.g. tabulating the study intervention characteristics and comparing against the planned groups for each synthesis (item #5)).

units.title: Reporting bias assessment
units.text: Describe any methods used to assess risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis (arising from reporting biases).

units.title: Certainty assessment
units.text: Describe any methods used to assess certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for an outcome.

units.title: Study selection
units.text: Describe the results of the search and selection process, from the number of records identified in the search to the number of studies included in the review, ideally using a flow diagram (see fig 1).

units.title: Study characteristics
units.text: Cite each included study and present its characteristics.

units.title: Risk of bias in studies
units.text: Present assessments of risk of bias for each included study.

units.title: Results of individual studies
units.text: For all outcomes, present, for each study: (a) summary statistics for each group (where appropriate) and (b) an effect estimate and its precision (e.g. confidence/credible interval), ideally using structured tables or plots.

units.title: Results of syntheses
units.text: For each synthesis, briefly summarise the characteristics and risk of bias among contributing studies.

units.title: Reporting biases
units.text: Present assessments of risk of bias due to missing results (arising from reporting biases) for each synthesis assessed.

units.title: Certainty of evidence
units.text: Present assessments of certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for each outcome assessed.

units.title: Discussion
units.text: Provide a general interpretation of the results in the context of other evidence.

units.title: Registration and protocol
units.text: Provide registration information for the review, including register name and registration number, or state that the review was not registered.

units.title: Support
units.text: Describe sources of financial or non-financial support for the review, and the role of the funders or sponsors in the review.

units.title: Competing interests
units.text: Declare any competing interests of review authors.

units.title: Availability of data, code, and other materials
units.text: Report which of the following are publicly available and where they can be found: template data collection forms; data extracted from included studies; data used for all analyses; analytic code; any other materials used in the review.
